posts.title: Bruno's Four Nights in the Linden Suite
posts.excerpt: The Varga family brought their 39 kg Bernese mountain dog Bruno to Alder Bay for four relaxed nights in the Linden Suite.
posts.content:
When the Varga family began planning their coastal holiday, their first concern was whether Bruno would truly be welcome. At 39 kg, Bruno is an affectionate, deep-chested Bernese mountain dog whose size often complicates family travel. In many hotels, travelling with a large dog means endless phone calls, awkward special exemptions, or being relegated to cramped quarters. When the Vargas discovered Ashiato Hotel, they found their questions answered clearly before they even had to ask. Our house rules openly state a 40 kg weight limit and welcome up to two dogs per room. As the Varga family noted in our guest register, they always asked first, but here the answer was on the website.

The family reserved the Linden Suite, our family room designed for up to four guests alongside their dogs. Situated inside our 1931 guesthouse at 7 Linden Row, the suite provides a spacious retreat of light oak flooring, comfortable seating, and clear views across Alder Bay. When the family arrived during check-in hours between 15:00 and 20:00, founder Ines Moreau immediately came over and knelt on the lobby floor to greet Bruno face to face. Beside the reception desk, Bruno found a fresh bowl of water and received a house-baked welcome biscuit prepared fresh that morning in the terrace kitchen by Rafael Ortiz.

Inside the Linden Suite, housekeeper Theo Brandt had arranged all eight standard amenities for their four nights by the coast. Bruno settled onto a clean dog bed with its own blanket, placed neatly beside two ceramic bowls and a stack of clean towels. Ines and Theo ensure every dog bed is thoroughly washed between guests, so arriving dogs find spotless bedding waiting for them. The family appreciated that the room accommodated Bruno's size with ease, giving him ample room to stretch out across the floor without blocking doorways or furniture.

Each morning began in our 1,200 square metre dog run, open daily from 06:00 to 22:00. Bruno enjoyed early romps across the damp grass, secure behind the 1.4-metre fence and double gate. Later, the family joined other guests on the terrace for breakfast between 07:30 and 10:00, with Bruno resting calmly under their table on his lead beside a fresh water bowl. In the evenings, the terrace reopened from 18:00 to 21:00 for drinks by the sea, offering a quiet place to unwind before bed.

The Vargas also made full use of our printed walking guide, following all three local routes during their stay. They completed the 2.4-kilometre Linden Loop in 35 minutes, took on the 4.1-kilometre Bay Dunes path, and enjoyed a long morning exploring the 6-kilometre Alder Woods trail. Returning with sandy paws, they used our entrance paw-wash station with warm water and fresh towels before heading inside. When the family stepped out for an evening dinner, dog sitter Hana Lindqvist stayed with Bruno in the suite, ensuring he remained relaxed and comfortable.

On their final evening, Kofi Mensah stopped to say goodbye during his 21:30 inspection round of the dog run before the gates closed at 22:00. At departure the following morning at 11:00, Ines Moreau saw the family off at the front desk. Having booked through Mei Chen with a simple 20% deposit, the family noted how refreshing it was to find a hotel where travelling with a large dog required no apologies or compromises. For Bruno and the Varga family, Ashiato was a place where dogs are genuinely expected and warmly welcomed.
